newsitem.title: USA: Northfield sees fall plant groundbreaking.
newsitem.headline: Northfield sees fall plant groundbreaking.

text.p: Northfield Laboratories Inc said Tuesday it expects to break ground this fall on a manufacturing plant for PolyHeme, a blood substitute that is undergoing pivotal Phase III clinical trials.
Addressing institutional investors at a conference here sponsored by Alex Brown & Co, Northfield said it expects to begin marketing PolyHeme in 1999.
"With an intended product launch in 1999, we also anticipate entering into a marketing and distribution arrangement with a strategic partner," said chief executive and chairman Richard DeWoskin.
He said Northfiled would like to have a partner in place at least a year prior to product launch.

"Over the next 12 months, we expect to finalize such an agreement with one or possibly more of the parties with whom we have had ongoing discussions for worldwide distribution of PolyHeme," he added. "Until then, we are well positioned financially to accomplish all of our objectives without the need for additional capital prior to a product launch."
Arch-rival Baxter International Inc announced Tuesday it has filed an application for marketing clearance for its blood substitute product, HemAssist, with the European Medicine Evaluations Agency.
